title: Zomato: Missing Items in Food Delivery
customer_persona: Hangry customer who waited 45 minutes for their dinner, only to find the main course missing.
context: Customer placed a multi-item order on Zomato from a local restaurant. The invoice shows full payment captured for every item, but when the bag was opened at home, the main course was missing. They reported it through the app's Help flow within a couple of hours, attaching a photo of what actually arrived, and want to know whether they'll get the missing item redelivered or refunded, and how much comes back and in what form. They're anxious because the reporting window closes fast and Zomato mediates with the restaurant before approving anything, which feels like a delay for a problem that wasn't their fault.
key_issues: One or more paid-for items missing from an otherwise-delivered order
Short post-delivery reporting window to file the complaint (photo evidence strengthens the claim)
Redelivery isn't realistic once the order has already been delivered — resolution is item-level refund, not resend
Resolution requires restaurant-side confirmation before refund is finalized
Uncertainty over refund amount (item-level vs full order) and refund mode/timeline (wallet credit vs original payment method)
resolution_path: Cross-check the invoice and photo evidence, log it as a missing-item case against the restaurant, and issue a partial item-level refund to the original payment method or wallet credit rather than arranging redelivery.

title: AWS: Billing Double Charge on EC2 Upgrades
customer_persona: Professional DevOps engineer. Upgraded their EC2 instances but was charged twice on their corporate credit card.
context: Customer opened a billing support case after noticing their latest AWS invoice listed two separate EC2-Instances line items covering the exact same billing period and dollar amount, even though the EC2 console shows only one running instance. The extra amount has already been drafted from their linked payment card, so they're frustrated about the cash-flow hit and confused because they never launched a second instance. They want AWS to explain the discrepancy and get a corrected invoice or credit before the next billing cycle closes.
key_issues: Duplicate line item for identical EC2 usage/amount in the same billing period
Mismatch between EC2 console (1 running instance) and the invoice (2 charged instances)
Payment already collected against the inflated invoice, creating urgency
Unclear root cause: billing pipeline glitch vs. Reserved Instance/On-Demand overlap vs. an untracked resource
Customer wants a corrected invoice or account credit, not just an explanation
resolution_path: Cross-reference the disputed line items against Cost Explorer / Cost and Usage Report data and the actual instance IDs and usage windows, and if a genuine billing-system error is confirmed, escalate to the billing team to issue a corrected invoice or service credit.

title: Stripe: API Payment Failed But Money Deducted
customer_persona: Anxious e-commerce store owner using Stripe. A customer tried to pay, the API returned an error, but the customer's bank account was deducted.
context: Customer tried to check out on a merchant's Stripe-powered store and got a card-declined error at the payment step — the API returned a failed PaymentIntent and no order was created. A few minutes later they check their banking app and see the full order amount sitting as a pending transaction or authorization hold, and conclude they were charged for something that never went through. They're anxious that money is missing from their available balance and want to know exactly when they'll get it back.
key_issues: Bank-side pending hold/authorization visible even though the payment API shows the charge as failed
Customer conflates a temporary authorization hold with an actual debit — no funds were actually captured
Hold typically caused by the issuer approving initial authorization before the gateway's own risk check declines it downstream
Release timeline is controlled entirely by the customer's card-issuing bank, not by the merchant or gateway
Customer worry about reduced available balance and fear of being double-charged if they retry the payment
resolution_path: Confirm via the dashboard/API that no successful charge exists, explain that this is a temporary issuer-side authorization hold rather than an actual charge, and advise the customer to wait for the standard 3-5 business day auto-release window before contacting their card issuer directly.

title: Vercel: Production Deployment Failing (404)
customer_persona: Stressed frontend developer who pushed a critical hotfix to Vercel, but the production build is resulting in a 404 for all users.
context: Customer's team merged a small config change to main this morning and the Vercel deployment shows Ready — the build log is clean, no errors — but the production domain now returns a 404 on every route except the homepage, right as their checkout flow is getting live traffic. They already tried the dashboard Redeploy button twice with no change and are convinced the platform itself is broken. They're on a paid plan, losing orders every minute the site is down, and are demanding either an immediate explanation or an immediate rollback, whichever is faster.
key_issues: Deployment status is Ready (build succeeded) but production routes 404
Likely mismatch between build-time routing metadata and actual output — commonly a wrong Output Directory, Framework Preset, or Root Directory in a monorepo
Customer redeployed twice without diagnosing the config, so the same broken settings keep reproducing the 404
Revenue-impacting outage on checkout pages during business hours is driving urgency for immediate rollback over root-cause diagnosis
Customer is unaware of Instant Rollback eligibility rules and how a rollback affects env vars and future auto-deploys
resolution_path: Compare the raw deployment URL against the custom domain to rule out DNS, check the Output tab and Runtime Logs filtered to 404s to pinpoint the misconfiguration, perform an Instant Rollback to the last known-good production deployment to restore service immediately, then walk the customer through fixing the setting before re-promoting.

title: Swiggy Instamart: Rotten Groceries Delivered
customer_persona: Annoyed customer who ordered fresh groceries via Swiggy Instamart. The fruits delivered are completely rotten and unusable.
context: Customer ordered milk and fresh vegetables through Swiggy Instamart and, on opening the delivery, found the milk curdled/sour and part of the produce visibly rotten well before the printed expiry date. The customer had already discarded the spoiled milk before thinking to photograph it, and is worried support will use the lack of photo evidence to deny the claim, especially since a similar complaint a few weeks ago was only met with an apology and no refund. They want a full refund, not a same-day replacement, since a fresh item from the same source can't be trusted either.
key_issues: Perishable item (milk/dairy, vegetables) delivered spoiled or rotten ahead of its printed expiry date
Item already discarded before the customer thought to take photo evidence
Prior similar spoiled-item complaint was denied or only met with an apology, eroding trust
Customer skeptical of a same-day replacement given an apparent cold-chain/storage failure at the source
Underlying food-safety concern beyond just a refund (recurring issue, near-expiry stock)
resolution_path: Validate the order and delivery timestamp, accept the customer's clear description of visible spoilage as sufficient even without a photo since the item was discarded for food-safety reasons, process a full refund rather than a replacement, and log a quality/cold-chain escalation against the fulfilling dark store.

title: Cloudflare: Custom Domain SSL Provisioning Stuck
customer_persona: Frustrated tech-savvy user. Trying to host a secure site on Cloudflare but getting security warnings for 24 hours.
context: Customer added a custom domain to their Cloudflare zone two days ago ahead of a product launch, and the edge SSL certificate for it has been stuck in Pending Validation (TXT) ever since, so the hostname is proxied through Cloudflare but serves an untrusted certificate, throwing browser security warnings on the checkout page. The customer insists they created the DNS validation record exactly as shown in the dashboard, but the status hasn't changed in over 24 hours. They're on a lower-tier plan without an SLA-backed support queue, so they're anxious this will keep blocking their launch.
key_issues: Edge SSL certificate stuck in Pending Validation (TXT) well past the normal issuance window
Domain may be on a partial (CNAME) setup rather than full nameserver delegation, so validation requires a manually-placed TXT record
Possible restrictive CAA record blocking the issuing certificate authorities
TXT record possibly placed on the wrong label, or a conflicting CNAME on the same _acme-challenge label
Site shows browser SSL warnings during a time-sensitive launch, with no fast SLA-backed support response
resolution_path: Confirm the zone's setup type and expected validation token, have the customer verify the TXT record's name/value and check for CA-blocking CAA records, correct any misplaced record, and manually re-trigger validation or reissue the certificate rather than waiting on the automatic retry cycle.

title: Uber: Driver Refused Duty and Was Abusive
customer_persona: Furious and shaken passenger whose Uber driver refused to go to the drop location and verbally abused them.
context: A rider took an evening Uber trip home and, partway through the ride, the driver became verbally aggressive after a disagreement over the route — raising his voice, making the rider feel intimidated, and continuing to drive erratically even after being asked to calm down. The rider ended the trip early once it felt safe to do so, got out, and submitted an in-app safety report immediately afterward. They're upset, want confirmation the report is actually being reviewed by a real person, and want assurance they will never be paired with this driver again.
key_issues: Driver verbal aggression/hostility during an active trip
Unsafe or erratic driving reported alongside the verbal incident
Rider uncertain whether the in-app report reaches a human safety reviewer
Rider wants guaranteed non-matching with the same driver going forward
Possible fare adjustment for a trip cut short due to safety concerns
resolution_path: A trust & safety agent reviews the trip's GPS/timestamp data, follows up with the rider directly, logs the incident against the driver's record for pattern review, confirms the rider will not be re-matched with that driver, and separately processes a fare adjustment for the shortened trip.

title: Shopify: Black Friday Discount Code Failing
customer_persona: Panicked Shopify store owner. Their Black Friday discount code is failing for all customers at checkout.
context: A customer tried to use the sale code during a merchant's one-day flash sale, but checkout rejected it or the price never dropped right as sale traffic peaked. They're frustrated because the promo banner advertised the discount and they'd already spent time filling their cart, and they're worried the deal will expire before support replies. Some customers complete the purchase anyway at full price and want the difference credited; others abandon the cart and demand the code be fixed immediately.
key_issues: Discount's storewide or per-customer redemption limit was reached mid-sale, so it still shows Active in admin but is correctly rejecting new uses
Cart didn't satisfy conditions attached to the code (minimum spend, eligible collection, or customer segment requirement)
Code isn't configured to combine with an automatic sale discount or another code already in the cart
High checkout traffic caused caching/latency glitches, or the discount field was hidden inside a collapsed mobile order-summary toggle
Customer already checked out at full price and is requesting a manual price adjustment or partial refund
resolution_path: Look up the specific discount in admin to confirm its active window, eligibility rules, redemption count, and combination settings against the customer's actual cart, and if the code should have applied, manually issue a partial refund or order edit for the discount difference.

title: Spotify: Premium Cancel + Retention Offer
customer_persona: Long-time subscriber who hit a billing dispute and now wants to cancel the family plan.
context: A Premium subscriber of just over four years contacts support after spotting a renewal charge on their card that they swear shouldn't have happened — they're certain they cancelled last month, but logging in shows Premium is still active and was billed again. They already tried disputing it informally and got what felt like a form-letter response, so now they want the charge refunded and the account cancelled outright, and they're explicit that they don't want to hear about any special offer to stay. Underneath the billing complaint is real fatigue: four years of on-time payments and this is how it's handled.
key_issues: Customer believes a prior cancellation was submitted but the subscription renewed and charged again anyway
Wants a refund for what they consider an erroneous charge
Demands confirmed, final cancellation rather than just a scheduled end-of-period downgrade
Long tenure raises expectation of goodwill/special handling
Preemptively refuses retention/discount offers and wants no upsell during the interaction
resolution_path: Verify whether the prior cancellation actually completed and confirm the billing owner (direct vs. app-store/carrier billing), issue a one-time goodwill refund if the charge was genuinely erroneous and direct-billed, explain that access is non-prorated so cancellation runs through the end of the paid period, then process the cancellation to a confirmed state and drop any retention offer entirely once declined.
